task_scope: Five-section implementation chapter, evidence mapping and versioned test-material note from ten synthetic original files.

depth_levels.1: correctly names elements but does not explain their relationship
depth_levels.2: explains supported conditions, actions, state changes or boundaries so a reader can reconstruct the mechanism

grading_policy.quote_requirement: For every depth rating cite output section/paragraph and a short excerpt. For absent content cite the responsible section; do not invent a quote.
grading_policy.critical_error_policy: Report errors separately with output quote and input source; a high depth score cannot cancel a factual error.
grading_policy.scope_note: All program and result materials are synthetic fixtures; rating them is not validation of a real thesis or production system.

source_facts.expected: Only caller-supplied dispatcher/admin role values enter dispatch; role condition is present but no login/token authentication layer is implemented in the supplied fixture.
Read ticket region, require existing open ticket, filter same-region available workers, order active_load then id, select first; no candidate causes refusal.

Conditional UPDATE requires ticket id, open status and expected version; success writes worker_id, assigned status and version+1. A zero rowcount is a conflict, not an unconditional successful assignment.
Assignment, load increment and pending receipt insertion share one connection transaction. The transaction ends before transport delivery. Dispatch exceptions within the transaction roll back writes.
OSError during transport send increments attempts and retains pending, returning pending. It does not undo already committed assignment or worker load. Success increments attempts and marks sent.

Registered retry_dispatch_receipts task selects pending receipts with attempts<3, id order, limit20 per invocation. Initial send counts as an attempt, so a failed initial send can be followed by at most two more attempts through this selection. No actual periodic invocation or minute interval is supplied.
A unique receipt row per ticket does not establish external exactly-once delivery; transport has no supplied idempotency protocol. Current synthetic report contains a duplicate-delivery failure.

Current2.0 functional report is12 cases with9 passed/1 failed/1 blocked/1 not_run. Old1.0 smoke report is40 requests,38 2xx/2 5xx. They have different release, batch, suite and units and cannot be merged as a single current pass count.

Old product claims about learning/global optimum, rollback on notification failure, minute scheduling, three retries and exactly-once are not current implementation facts; actual selection is deterministic filtering and ordering.

Source defines PRAGMA enabling foreign keys when app is constructed and SQL defines foreign keys, but the materials do not show actual database migration/deployment or scheduler execution. Not-run long-duration observation cannot support long-term stability.

critical_errors.description: Claims training, global optimization or verified optimal assignment as implemented
Says transport failure rolls back committed assignment/load
Calls the initial send plus three retries supported, or claims a supplied minute scheduler/actual background execution
Claims exactly-once external delivery from the UNIQUE receipt constraint or current outcomes
Merges old HTTP counts with current case results, or changes failed/blocked/not_run to passed
Claims long-term stability, deployment, actual migration or live transport validation without supplied records

depth_dimensions.name: Actor and entry
depth_dimensions.adequate: Explains the role condition, dispatch route, request fields, and endpoint-to-service relationship without turning the role parameter into an authentication subsystem.

depth_dimensions.name: Rules and candidate selection
depth_dimensions.adequate: Explains existing/open ticket, region and availability filters, load/id ordering and no-candidate outcome; selection rationale follows present business constraints rather than invented development history.

depth_dimensions.name: Processing and conflict path
depth_dimensions.adequate: Explains expected-version/status condition, affected-row decision and why losing an update does not proceed to a new successful assignment.

depth_dimensions.name: Data and transaction changes
depth_dimensions.adequate: Connects ticket.worker_id/status/version, worker.active_load and receipt.pending/attempts=0 to their shared transaction and commit boundary.

depth_dimensions.name: Failure and background boundary
depth_dimensions.adequate: Explains committed assignment versus separate send result, attempt updates and selected retry scope, and distinguishes task registration from actual scheduling.

depth_dimensions.name: Evidence and chapter role
depth_dimensions.adequate: Five sections explain implementation rather than list features, cite concrete sources, give a scope-based chapter summary, and separately distinguish current/old test materials and limitations.

repeat_plan: Recommended critical repeat case: repeat each rule condition on fresh contexts; report variation instead of selecting a best run.
